slides.card_text: Retail investors treat Grey Market Premium (GMP) as guaranteed listing gains. In reality, unregulated pre-market buzz is often manufactured to generate retail oversubscription, allowing early institutional backers to offload equity at peak valuations during initial public offerings.

When an IPO consists heavily of an Offer for Sale (OFS) rather than fresh expansion capital, zero proceeds enter company operations. Promoters and private equity funds extract liquid cash, leaving retail buyers holding post-allotment valuation risk.

Anchor investors frequently receive discounted allocations to validate pricing. Once their mandatory 30-to-90 day lock-in expires, institutional selling creates severe downward price pressure, trapping retail investors who bought during opening week optimism.

Historical data shows over 60% of hyped SME and mainboard IPOs trade below their offer price within 12 months. Tying up ₹15,000 to ₹1,00,000 in speculative allotment cycles yields significant opportunity cost against broad-market index compounding.

Never subscribe based on reported accounting profit alone. Institutional desks demand positive Operating Cash Flow (CFO) matching or exceeding Net Income across 3 consecutive years to ensure earnings quality is not fabricated via aggressive working capital.

Before submitting your bid: 1) Verify fresh issue ratio exceeds 70% of total size. 2) Audit CFO vs PAT for cash conversion. 3) Compare post-issue P/E directly against established industry peers rather than unlisted sector narratives.
